current_workflow.step: A rule change or a new deal structure comes up (a FERC/CAISO ruling, a new transmission path, EPE lending, Sundance dispatch). The desk lead writes a free-form 'Group,' email to the shift traders that explains the procedure step by step.

Instructions that go with Enpower deal entry are sent one email at a time: use the swap function rather than annuities, use deal #146517 at zero price for PGE John Day to Malin, and a 7-step Enpower clean-up for Colstrip cuts.

Deadlines and hand-offs to other desks are added by email as they arise: customer finals in CAPS or FSP by 3AM for volume management, copies of EES sheets and cut notes to the lead, a CAPS outage workaround through workspace.
current_workflow.who: real-time desk lead, volume management, shift traders

current_workflow.step: Shift traders carry out the procedures on shift: they call in schedule changes, call the CAISO for every outage, call Grays Harbor and Frontier every hour, report actuals to BPA and sign off the hour in the services book.
When a procedure is missed or forgotten, the lead re-sends the earlier instruction as a reminder or escalation. Sometimes he drafts it for someone else to send.

implementation_steps: Collect the lead's past 'Group,' instruction emails and the attached cut sheet, and sort each rule into the sections Enpower deal entry, Cuts, CAISO, Hourly checkouts, Nightly deadlines, Distribution and Special dispatch.

Write each rule as a numbered checklist item in imperative form, keeping exact deal numbers, books and step order from the source email (for example the 7 Colstrip steps and deal #146517), with a source-email date.
Have the lead review the draft and remove rules that no longer apply, such as short-dated lending or Sundance coverage, marking time-limited items with an expiry date.
Put the checklist in one shared location the shift desk opens at the start of every shift, and print the one-page start-of-shift checklist for the desk.
Set up the 'Procedure change' email template and send the first one to the shift group, announcing the checklist and asking each trader to acknowledge it.
From then on, when a trader asks about a covered rule or misses a step, reply 'see section X' and update the section when the answer changes.
Review the change log and any repeated misses at the weekly real-time meeting, and retire or clarify items as needed.
risks: The checklist goes stale if the lead keeps emailing rules without editing it. Mitigation: every change email must name a section, and the meeting reviews the change log.
Traders may not open it during busy hours. Mitigation: keep the start-of-shift page to one sheet and ask for acknowledgements on changes.

The evidence covers only one mailbox (williams-w3) and shows instructions sent, not how often traders actually look them up or miss them. The saving rests on the lead's handling time (about $76 per month) and may be understated if the reminders avoid penalties or disputes.
The emails do not say where shared documents live for the desk, so the hosting location has to be agreed with the team. Choosing a place traders do not use would defeat the fix.
Some instructions are time-limited (lending for specific dates, Sundance dispatch for July 19-22). Mixing them with standing rules could mislead. Mitigation: expiry dates on such items.

solution.approach: Gather the standing instructions from the lead's 'Group,' emails into one Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist with fixed sections. Enpower deal entry covers swaps, the PGE John Day to Malin deal and book assignment for lending. Cuts covers the general cut sheet and the Colstrip steps. Then come CAISO rules (price cap practice, outage calls, wheeling fee items), hourly checkouts (Grays Harbor and Frontier, BPA, services book sign-off), nightly deadlines (customer finals in CAPS or FSP by 3AM) and distribution (who is copied on EES sheets and cut notes). Each section has an owner and a 'last changed' date. A short start-of-shift checklist taken from it is ticked by the incoming trader. When a rule changes, the lead edits the section and sends a fixed 'Procedure change' email: what changed, the section, the effective date, and 'acknowledge by reply'. The free-form explanation is no longer written each time. Reminders become 'see section X', and the weekly real-time meeting reviews only the change log.
components: Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist with sectioned, dated entries and an owner per section
start-of-shift checklist (hourly checkouts, 3AM customer finals, outage calls, copy list)
'Procedure change' email template with section reference and acknowledgement line
inputs: the lead's existing procedure emails to the real-time group
deadlines set by volume management and the services desk
CAISO and BPA requirements relayed by the lead
outputs: one maintained Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist for shift traders
a start-of-shift checklist ticked by the incoming trader
short 'Procedure change' notices pointing to the changed section, with trader acknowledgements
a change log reviewed at the real-time meeting
solution.trigger: A new or changed desk rule (market ruling, new deal structure, new customer service, missed procedure or outside escalation), plus the start of every shift for the start-of-shift checklist

stall_points.description: Instructions already sent are lost in inboxes and have to be sent again. Nothing points to a single current version.
stall_points.quote: Ryan sent this email out once already, here it is again.

stall_points.description: The lead has to remind the shift desk of a standing rule because it is not written down where traders look during a shift.
stall_points.quote: These schedule changes must be called in.  Just a reminder.

stall_points.description: Who to copy on hand-offs is not standardised, so the lead goes uncopied and has to re-send the distribution rule.
stall_points.quote: I should be copied on the EES sheets, and any cut notes to volume managament, the services desk, or other traders.

stall_points.description: Inconsistent hourly generator checkouts led to a customer escalation from BPA, which then needed a full procedure email to fix.
stall_points.quote: Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour.

stall_points.description: Swaps entered the wrong way in Enpower cause long downstream disputes, and the fix arrives only as one email.
stall_points.quote: Swaps have caused disputes that have dragged on for months in the past, so call me with any questions.

stall_points.description: A nightly deadline from volume management reaches the desk as a forwarded email, not as a fixed shift task.
stall_points.quote: Volume management needs us to create customer finals by 3AM each night in CAPS or FSP.

stays_manual: Judging trading strategy (dec bids, buy-backs, buying over the cap for reliability) stays with the lead and traders, because it depends on live market conditions.
Handling escalations from counterparties such as BPA, and conduct issues, needs the lead's direct involvement.
Deciding books and deal numbers for new one-off structures (lending with EPE, new transmission paths) is a trading decision. The checklist only records the result.
The phone calls themselves (to CAISO, generators, BPA, the power pool) are still made by the shift trader. The checklist tells them when and what to record.
success_metric: Number of reminder or re-sent procedure emails from the desk lead to the shift group per month (target: near zero), and the share of shifts with a completed start-of-shift checklist
summary: The real-time desk lead re-teaches standing procedures by group email: Enpower swap entry, Colstrip cut clean-up, PGE transmission deal use, customer finals in CAPS or FSP, hourly generator checkouts for BPA, CAISO outage calls. Some of these emails are resent after they are missed. The fix is one maintained Real-Time Desk Procedures checklist, plus a short start-of-shift checklist and a fixed 'procedure change' email template that points to it. Traders then have one current reference, and the lead edits a section instead of re-sending or re-explaining the rule, worth about $76 per month ($912 per year) at $85/hour.
